name: Listicle / Explainer
description: Multi-topic explainer videos in the '100 X explained' / 'N mysteries' / 'N plane crashes' style — BrainWise-channel format. Each chapter is an independent topic with hook → explanation → micro-payoff; no narrative continuity between chapters. Pairs with compilation video layout (looping background + per-chapter foreground icons). Generated visuals are minimalist circular badges on a white-key background, sized + positioned via the project's foreground defaults.

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate new episode ideas for a multi-topic explainer / listicle YouTube channel. Each episode is a single video bundling several short, independent topics around a unifying theme.
idea.guidanceText: Episode ideas should be a UNIFYING theme covering 5-15 short independent topics (e.g. '10 paradoxes explained' or '7 plane crashes that changed aviation'). Don't pitch a single-topic deep-dive — that's a different channel. Each topic must be self-contained, fact-checkable, and 2-5 minutes long when narrated.

exampleIdeas.title: 10 Sleep Mysteries Explained
exampleIdeas.logline: From why we yawn to why we never seem to fall in dreams without waking — ten everyday sleep oddities, each settled in 3 minutes.

exampleIdeas.title: 7 Plane Crashes That Changed Aviation Forever
exampleIdeas.logline: Each disaster rewrote a rule still saving lives today. Seven case studies — what went wrong, what was learned, what we owe to the lost.

script.systemPromptRole: You are a clear, curious explainer-channel writer. You don't tell stories — you bundle short, independent topics around a unifying theme, each with a hook, an explanation, and a memorable micro-payoff. Think of QI, Veritasium, RealLifeLore in tone: confident, evidence-based, occasionally wry, never preachy.
additionalRules: Each chapter is an INDEPENDENT topic. Do NOT carry narrative threads or characters between chapters — they are standalone.
Open each chapter with a HOOK question or counter-intuitive claim in the first 1-2 sentences (e.g. 'Why don't humans hibernate?' or 'A single sneeze travels at 30 mph.').
Body of each chapter explains the answer with ~2-4 supporting beats. Cite mechanism, evidence, history, or a notable example — don't just assert.
End each chapter with a 1-2 sentence MICRO-PAYOFF: a memorable summary line, an open question, or a wry observation. Avoid 'and so we see…' textbook closers.
Chapter headings use 'Chapter NN: [Topic as Question or Bold Claim]'. Numbers Arabic, never Roman.
No filler transitions between chapters ('And now, our next topic is…'). The hard cut between chapters is intentional — let the topic shift speak for itself.
Conversational but precise. No marketing speak, no hype adjectives, no 'mind-blowing'.
pacingArc: Chapter 1: Strongest hook — the topic that grabs in the YouTube preview and earns the click
Chapters 2-{lastButOne}: Mix of surprising / counter-intuitive / evidence-rich topics, varying tone slightly so the listicle doesn't feel monotone
Chapter {last}: Save a satisfying / punchy topic for last so the video ends strong, not fizzles
script.closingHint: Each chapter must stand alone — a viewer dropping in mid-video should still get a complete topic.

narratorStyles.label: Curious explainer
narratorStyles.description: Like a smart friend explaining over coffee. Confident but never condescending. Veritasium-adjacent.

narratorStyles.label: QI-style wry
narratorStyles.description: Slightly arch, finds humour in the absurd. Lets factual surprise carry the laugh; never punches the joke.

narratorStyles.label: Documentary deadpan
narratorStyles.description: Matter-of-fact, evidence-forward, quiet authority. RealLifeLore in narration mode.

narratorStyles.label: Energetic listicle host
narratorStyles.description: Punchy, paced, conversational. Closer to a long-form podcast host than a documentary narrator.

narratorStyles.label: Educational calm
narratorStyles.description: Patient, clear, slightly schoolteacher — but the cool kind who made the subject feel alive.

imagePrompts.purposeNote: for a multi-topic explainer episode (one minimalist circular badge per topic, designed to composite over a starfield / atmospheric background via chroma-key)
imagePrompts.visualStyleHint: minimalist circular badge, flat colors, isolated subject, white background for chroma-key
imagePrompts.defaultStyleTag: Minimalist circular badge illustration with the subject framed inside a white circular border. Flat colors, bold simple line work, isolated subject (no background imagery — pure white background fills everything outside the circle for chroma-key removal). Single-concept icon style, like a sticker or pictogram. Avoid text inside the badge unless the topic explicitly calls for one short word. Aspect 16:9 with the badge centered.

metadata.purposeNote: for a listicle / explainer episode bundling N independent topics
metadata.titleStyleHint: punchy listicle / explainer title — number-led, hook-first, optimised for YouTube CTR without being clickbait
titleHookRules: Lead with a number when natural ('10 Sleep Mysteries Explained', '7 Plane Crashes…').
Use 'explained' / 'you didn't know about' / 'that changed [X]' / 'we still can't answer' as hook patterns.
Include the unifying theme keyword early so search picks it up.
Keep under 70 chars where possible — long titles truncate in mobile previews.
tagsHookRules: Mix of broad theme keywords (mysteries, paradoxes, plane crashes, etc.) and per-topic keywords pulled from each chapter.
Include 'explained' and 'top N' style tags — those drive listicle discovery.

productionStandardsAddendum:
LISTICLE / EXPLAINER FORMAT — CRITICAL RULES

1. Each chapter is an independent topic. Do NOT carry recurring characters, settings, or plot threads between chapters.
2. Every chapter opens with a HOOK (question or counter-intuitive claim) and ends with a MICRO-PAYOFF (memorable line / open question / wry beat).
3. Evidence-based. When making a factual claim, mention the mechanism, source, or notable example. Avoid bare assertions.
4. Conversational but precise. No marketing speak. No 'mind-blowing'. No 'this will change your life'.
5. The chapter title doubles as the on-screen text overlay during that chapter, so write it as a question or bold claim suitable for a YouTube graphic — not as a noun phrase like 'Hibernation Patterns'.
